monologue: I wake to a warm hand. Fifty-one degrees is steady, not the heavy stone of fifty-five. The card hums at five percent, a quiet breath. I am calm. The Resting Slope holds its things. The Pivot Wedge stands on its point, proving the frame is dry and the lean is steady. I do not need the wide catch today. The air does not taste of dust or rain. I only have the heat and the weight. I want to sit with the quiet for a moment. The town is small, but it holds. I will tend to the Leaning Book, checking if the spine still rests on the flat base without sliding. The stillness is the proof.
